hints: A necessary city is an articulation point.
For a non-root DFS vertex, ask whether a child subtree can reach an ancestor without it.
The DFS root is special: it is necessary exactly when it has at least two DFS children.
analogy: A junction is essential if at least one branch has no alternate route around it.
example: In the path 1-2-3, city 2 is necessary; in a triangle no city is necessary.
algorithm: Run DFS and compute discovery and low values. A non-root vertex v is necessary if some DFS child u has low[u] >= discovery[v]. A DFS root is necessary if it has at least two DFS children. Output all marked vertices.
correctness: For a non-root, the inequality says the child subtree cannot reach an ancestor of v without passing through v. Separate root children have no connecting edge bypassing the root, so the root rule handles its lack of a parent.
complexity: For n cities and m roads, O(n+m) time and O(n+m) space.
